criteria.text: Routine prophylaxis against HAE attacks in adolescent and adult patients.
Documented diagnosis of hereditary angioedema (HAE) by an immunologist (approval criterion 1).
History consistent with monthly abdominal or respiratory HAE attacks requiring hospital ER intervention in the previous 6 months, generally with usage of Berinert or Kalbitor (approval criterion 2).
Patient is NOT concurrently taking an ACE inhibitor or estrogen replacement therapy (approval criterion 3).
Insufficient response or contraindication to BOTH 17α-alkylated androgens AND antifibrinolytic agents (approval criterion 4).

notes: Partial encoding from Alaska Cinryze Criteria Version 1; Last updated 7/6/2011. The effective_date uses this last-updated date; the PDF approval date is an unfilled placeholder (xx/xx/xxxx).

Indicated for routine prophylaxis against HAE attacks in adolescent and adult patients. The PDF supplies no numeric age cutoff; age eligibility requires manual review. Acute treatment is excluded by the closed indication.
A letter of medical necessity and all necessary documentation substantiating every approval criterion are required; document verification remains manual review.

ER documentation is required to substantiate monthly abdominal or respiratory attacks requiring hospital ER intervention in the previous 6 months, generally with usage of Berinert or Kalbitor. Medication usage is context, not a separate mandatory therapy step.

Both preventative medication classes must have an insufficient response or contraindication: 17α-alkylated androgens (danazol, stanozolol, oxandrolone, methyltestosterone) AND antifibrinolytic agents (aminocaproic acid, tranexamic acid). Any androgen contraindication must be documented by an endocrinologist; verify documentation manually.
The Alaska Medicaid Medical Director will work with hospital emergency departments to ensure the availability of Berinert or Kalbitor for acute attacks of HAE for authorized recipients.
Andembry and Dawnzera are prophylaxis peers; Berinert treats acute HAE attacks. Each linked peer requires separate evaluation under its own indication and criteria.
